Fetal Echo Project · Unit D1 · Detect tier · v0.1

The normal heart in five views

DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

You will be able to

  • Name the five planes of the screening examination in order.
  • State what must be established before looking at the heart.
  • Give the normal values for heart size, axis and rate.
  • Explain why counting four chambers is not a normal four-chamber view.

Why five views

A screening scan does not need to name the lesion. It needs to answer one question reliably: is this heart normal? The five-view sweep is the shortest route to that answer.

Screening built on the four-chamber view alone misses lesions that only show in the great arteries. Adding outflow-tract and great-vessel views has improved detection.1

Current guidance asks for situs, the four-chamber view, and the outflow-tract and great-vessel views in every screening examination, ideally between 18 and 22 weeks.2,3

The sweep

The examination is one continuous movement through five planes, from the upper abdomen to the upper chest: situs, four-chamber view, left ventricular outflow tract, right ventricular outflow tract with the three-vessel view, and the three-vessel-and-trachea view.4

Think of it as a sweep, not five photographs. What matters is how each plane turns into the next.

Before the heart: left, right and situs

First work out which side of the fetus is left and which is right. Only then assess situs.5

With normal situs, the upper-abdomen plane shows the stomach on the left, the descending aorta to the left of the spine, and the inferior vena cava in front of and to the right of the spine.6

Size, position, axis, rate

A normal heart fills about a third of the chest.7

It sits mostly in the left chest, with its long axis pointing left at about 45 degrees. The accepted range is 20 degrees either side.8

The rate is 120 to 160 beats per minute and regular. A rate that stays below 110 needs prompt specialist review for possible heart block.9,10

More than a count

Seeing four chambers, or three vessels, is not the same as a normal view. Each view is judged against specific criteria.11

Colour Doppler and checklists

The 2023 guideline encourages colour Doppler in screening and recommends working from a checklist, with quality assurance of the examination.12
